text:
alex: quick q — started seeing 401s from our service in k8s when using mounted secret file for API key. works locally. headers show Authorization: Basic <token>. any tips?
marie: do you mean you mount a file and read it at startup?
alex: yeah, we mount /etc/secrets/redwood_key, read it into process.env.REDWOOD_KEY via entrypoint script
sam: common gotcha: file contains trailing CRLF/os newline. that breaks base64 if you include it in the input to Buffer.from. try trim()
alex: ah — using `key = fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` then `Buffer.from(key + ':').toString('base64')`... forgot trim
alex: example:
```
const key = fs.readFileSync('/etc/secrets/redwood_key', 'utf8').trim();
const header = 'Authorization: Basic ' + Buffer.from(key + ':').toString('base64');
```

jordan: also check there's no BOM. `sed -n '1p' /etc/secrets/redwood_key | tr -d '\r'` in your init container can sanitize
sam: fwiw we updated our Go SDK to accept raw key and do the Basic wrapping internally, but older clients expect you to build header
marie: alternative: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var from Secret Manager (single-line) rather than mount file
alex: testing now...
ci-bot: automated test run: 1 failed (401) 2 passed
alex: ok trim fixed it, 401 gone :tada: thanks
jordan: filing tiny doc blurb in devex README about mounting secrets + trim + no-bom
alex: assigning to @marie to add snippet
marie: on it, will open PR with examples for node/go/k8s
sam: optional follow-up: SDK patch to accept key with newline and normalize — think worth it?
marie: yes, safer. i'll draft follow-up change and link ticket
alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
